The number of Fubini rankings of length $n$ that produce a given parking outcome $\pi$ depends only on the number $k$ of ascending runs of $\pi$.  Each ascending run of length $r$ can be split into blocks at any of its $r\!-\!1$ internal gaps, giving $2^{r-1}$ possibilities, and the choices for different runs are independent.  Hence the total number of rankings is  

\[
\prod_{\text{run}} 2^{\,(\text{length of run})-1}=2^{\left(\sum \text{run lengths}\right)-k}=2^{\,n-k}.
\]

**Answer:** $2^{\,n-k}$.

ANSWER: $2^{\,n-k}$
